dedupe_keys.name: unlocking digital growth the role of internet exchange points in south east europe ripe ncc october 2025

description: This RIPE NCC report reviews the Internet exchange point landscape in South East Europe (Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Montenegro, Albania, North Macedonia, Kosovo, Bulgaria, Romania and Greece) and applies four criteria for IXP success: keeping local traffic local, supporting local interconnection for the digital economy, attracting global cloud and content players, and becoming hubs for regional traffic exchange. It notes that the region's IXPs differ widely in maturity, from one established three decades ago to many started in the last decade, and in governance, from university-led initiatives to commercial businesses. Chapters cover connecting service providers, content localisation, membership policy, hyperscaler attraction and regional connectivity, with recommendations, an operator matrix and a content matrix dated March 2025. Producer: RIPE NCC, October 2025, 33 pages. Coverage: eleven economies in South East Europe. Access: free PDF; the executive summary, contents and background were read, the chapters were not read in full. Licence and cost: free; licence not stated. Caveats: the matrices are a snapshot for March 2025 and no machine-readable data is provided. Simulation uses: the benchmarking criteria and operator and content matrices support interconnection capacity-planning scenarios. Related records: the Euro-IX IXP database (data-euro-ix-ixp-database) and the PCH IXP directory (data-pch-ixp-directory).
